To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) traveling waves of cell signaling can be mediated by extracellular ligand release and (ii) such waves can exhibit nonmonotonic dependence of speed of propagation on diffusivity of extracellular ligands.

in systems with autocrine signal transmission with ligand degradation, the speed of wave propagation can be non-monotonic function of the ligand diffusion rate and that the speed of wave initiation is proportional to the square root of the ligand degradation rate.

traveling waves of cell signaling mediated by extracellular ligand release and diffusion can exhibit non-monotonic speed–diffusivity dependence and that the speed of propagation can depend strongly on the receptor density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of extracellular ligand in the propagation of traveling waves of cell communication.

the mathematical modeling of traveling waves in epithelial layers that are mediated by autocrine loops with extracellular ligands.

the positive feedback autocrine loop with extracellular ligands and ligand degradation leads to traveling waves of cell signaling with a number of unusual features.

the positive feedback autocrine signaling loops with extracellular ligands can lead to the formation of traveling waves that can exhibit unusual properties and that the properties of such waves can be used to infer the properties of the underlying biophysical processes.

the positive feedback autocrine signaling can lead to the formation of traveling waves in epithelial layers, even in the absence of any active transport of the ligand.

we developed a biophysical model for autocrine signaling with extracellular ligands and analyzed the problem with the positive feedback nonlinearities, focusing on the traveling wave solutions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the speed of traveling waves in the systems with autocrine signal transmission can exhibit non-monotonic behavior as a function of the diffusion coefficient of the diffusible signal, which can lead to the existence of a critical diffusivity below which the traveling wave cannot exist.
the extracellular mode of ligand degradation is an important factor that should be considered in the analysis of traveling waves of cell signaling.
the extracellular degradation can play a key role in the dynamics of traveling waves in autocrine systems.
